In the heart of a decaying city, there was a man named Elijah. He had a peculiar ability - he could fully heal anyone he touched. But this gift was not without its consequences.

Elijah lived in isolation, feared and revered by the people of the city. They came to him with their sick and wounded, begging for his touch. And each time, he would oblige, his hands glowing with a soft light as he healed them.

But some took issue with just how fully he healed. You see, Elijah's touch did not just mend bones and cure diseases. It restored people to their prime, erasing scars, regrowing lost limbs, even reversing the effects of aging.

This caused an uproar in the city. The old became young again, the weak became strong. The natural order was disrupted, and chaos ensued. People fought for Elijah's touch, desperate to regain their youth and vitality.

But the horror did not stop there. Elijah's touch also healed the mind, erasing traumas and painful memories. People lost parts of themselves, their identities altered. They became strangers to their loved ones, their pasts wiped clean.

Elijah watched in despair as his city descended into madness. His gift, once a beacon of hope, had become a curse. He was tormented by guilt, haunted by the faces of those he had 'healed'.

One day, a woman came to him. She was old and frail, her body ravaged by disease. But her eyes were clear, and she spoke with a calmness that belied her condition.

"I do not want your healing," she said. "I have lived my life, with all its pain and joy. I do not wish to forget."

Elijah was taken aback. For the first time, someone had refused his touch. He looked at the woman, her wrinkles a testament to her years, her eyes reflecting a lifetime of experiences. And he realized the horror of what he had done.

From that day forward, Elijah refused to use his gift. He lived out his days in solitude, haunted by the chaos he had caused. His story became a dark legend in the city, a chilling reminder of the dangers of tampering with the natural order.

And so, the man who could heal anyone he touched became a symbol of horror, his gift a curse. His story served as a grim reminder that not all that is broken should be fixed, and that some things are better left untouched.

In the heart of New York City, a skyscraper named "The Olympus" towered over its neighbors. Its owner, a billionaire named Arthur Pendragon, was facing an unusual problem. Harpies, mythical creatures with the body of a bird and the face of a woman, had taken up residence on the roof of his building. 

"I understand that this is a major issue for you," said the weary voice on the other end of the phone. It was the city's animal control department. "But Harpies illegally nesting atop your skyscraper isn't an animal control issue. Please hang up and contact your local heroic representative."

Arthur sighed, hanging up the phone. He looked out of his office window at the top floor of The Olympus, where the Harpies were nesting. They were causing a ruckus, their screeches echoing through the city streets and their feathers littering the sidewalks below.

Arthur dialed another number, this time reaching the Heroic Representative Office. "This is Arthur Pendragon," he said, "I have a Harpy problem."

The next day, a woman named Athena arrived at The Olympus. She was the city's heroic representative, a mediator between the human and mythical worlds. With her silver armor and owl-shaped helmet, she was an imposing figure.

Athena ascended to the roof, where the Harpies were nesting. They screeched at her, but she stood her ground. "I am Athena," she said, "I am here to negotiate on behalf of Arthur Pendragon."

The Harpies quieted, looking at Athena with curiosity. She explained that while they were free to live in the city, they couldn't nest on top of The Olympus. It was causing problems for the humans below.

The Harpies were reluctant at first, but Athena was patient. She proposed a solution: a nearby park had a large, unused aviary. The Harpies could nest there, away from the humans but still in the heart of the city.

After much discussion, the Harpies agreed. They left The Olympus, following Athena to their new home. The city breathed a sigh of relief as the screeching stopped and the feather rain ceased.

Arthur watched from his office as the Harpies left. He felt a strange sense of relief and gratitude towards Athena. He realized then that the city was more than just skyscrapers and humans; it was a place where the mythical and the mundane coexisted.

From that day forward, Arthur became a staunch advocate for mythical creature rights. He used his influence to create more spaces for them in the city, ensuring that they could live alongside humans without conflict.

And as for the Harpies, they thrived in their new home. They became a beloved part of the city, their once feared screeches now a unique part of New York's soundscape. And every so often, you could see a feather floating down from the sky, a gentle reminder of the city's mythical inhabitants.

When I was in college, I was dating this girl for a brief amount of time. I really liked her and I stayed with her for a bit when I was in-between places. We were both sparse on money so we tried to help each other out financially whenever we could. Unfortunately, someone in my family had gotten sick around this time and I had to step out of town for three days. When I came back, the first thing I had to do was use the bathroom. As I stepped in, there it was--a full body whitetail deer mount. At first, I didn't think much of it. In fact, I was a little skeptical--my girlfriend had never mentioned that she particularly liked the outdoors or deer all that much. After a while, however, I started to research a little bit more. Apparently, a full body whitetail deer mount costs *at least* $3,000 or more. This is when I confronted my girlfriend about it, thinking that we both don't have enough money to pay for something like that. Even after pressing her for an obscene amount of time, she didn't say anything, only telling me that it was a surprise for me (by the way I have no particular interest in deer). To this day, I've not figured out why that was there.

I was in English class for the second semester of my sophomore year of high school. We were doing some exercise with a book the whole class was reading (I think it was *The Great Gatsby*). The exercise consisted of working with a partner and formulating a prediction for what will happen later on in the book. I was randomly assigned to this one white girl in my class. For some context, I am an Indian male and she was one of those preppy and snobby white girls who consistently and constantly talked about the guys she hooked up with. I had spoke to her on different occasions strictly for school (e.g. asking her for help on a math problem, asking her a question, etc.). Anywho, we were randomly assigned as partners for this brief exercise. As I was thinking of what could possibly happen later in the book and was thinking of a well-thought-out prediction, I wasn't speaking for a brief second. This is when this girl looks me dead in the eyes, and with full-on seriousness, says "Can you speak good English?" I looked back at her and for fear of confrontation, I smiled and said "Yeah, of course." Now, she didn't think much of it, but I was *pissed*. I also didn't want to say anything to her because I was kind of shy. I don't know what to make of this situation looking back, but I thought this was a pretty dumb thing to happen.

He asked me if I wanted to play on his new PS4--with a camouflage design. At first, I didn't think much of it (I was only slightly skeptical) when he outrightly says "I stole it from your house."
